<thought>Based on the mass spectrum (M+H = 262.099) the neutral mass is ~261.092 Da. The 13C NMR shows 16 distinct carbon signals, including a carbonyl carbon (~166 ppm) and a methoxy carbon (~52 ppm), indicating a methoxy‑substituted aromatic carbonyl compound with roughly 17 carbons and 3 oxygens (C₁₇H₁₀O₃). This fits a highly unsaturated structure such as a methoxy‑substituted anthracenone. A plausible SMILES that matches this formula and the NMR pattern is “COc1ccc2c(c1)C(=O)c3ccccc3c2”. This corresponds to 1‑methoxy‑9‑anthracenone (C₁₇H₁₀O₃). 

<final_answer>COc1ccc2c(c1)C(=O)c3ccccc3c2</final_answer>
